Alex: Quick idea — prototype an inline sampling window inside the worker loop to catch bad kernel selections and KV-cache churn, but keep production overhead < 2%.
Maya: Curious how "inline" differs from our current sampled-trace approach. You mean sampling periods aligned to batching boundaries?
Alex: Exactly. Instead of full nsys runs we open a short sampling window on a subset of workers for N seconds, annotate with NVTX, then merge timelines. That keeps disruption local.
Jorge: Implementation sketch:
```
// on worker start
if (rand() < sample_prob) {
  enable_sampling_window(duration_ms=2000);
}
// add NVTX around hot paths
nvtxRangePushA("select_kernel");
selectKernel(...);
nvtxRangePop();
```
Sam: Nice. What are the overhead numbers from your lab run?
Alex: Local bench (T4, small-batch workloads):
- full nsys trace on 100% traffic -> p95 latency +35-60% (very noisy)
- 1% sampled windows (2s every 200s) -> observed ~1.3% median CPU overhead, +3ms p95 tail in worst case
- 5% sampling -> ~5-6% overhead for CPU side, GPU timeline size blows up
Maya: That matches my earlier notes: full traces kill throughput and mess with kernel scheduling. Sampling wins if we can correlate with NVTX markers.
Devon: How do we avoid biasing selection? If sampling windows coincide with cold-cache builds or orthogonal traffic, we might get false positives.
Jorge: Two ideas:
- stagger windows per worker to avoid alignment
- only sample when load is within normal operating band (e.g., rate within 10-90% of norm)
Sam: Also cap sampling "budget" per minute per pool so it can't exceed X% of requests. We should also ensure feature-flag off for P0 customers.
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary trace-run scheduled: trace-proxy v0.6 -> infra/trace-runner (id: cr-442)
Maya: For tooling, we'll use nsys + perfetto import. Command I used:
```
nsys profile --output trace.qdrep --trace=cuda,osrt,drv --sample=cpu:100 --duration 2s --force-overwrite
``` 
Then convert qdrep -> perfetto and open in UI, NVTX ranges show kernel selection boundaries.
Alex: Important: measure overhead from two angles — added latency per request and added noise in kernel timelines (i.e., changed launch ordering). In our tests, short windows have much less perturbation than long full traces.
Devon: KV cache specifics: we need to capture whether eviction patterns appear during windows. Suggest adding a lightweight counter event on cache miss/hit with NVTX so GPU timeline can be correlated.
Jorge: Agree. Something like `nvtxRangePushA("kv:miss")` on miss. Keep these markers extremely cheap.
Sam: Guardrails proposal:
- max sampling traffic 2% by default (configurable)
- disable sampling if p95 increases > 10ms during ramp
- no sampling on dedicated enterprise nodes unless explicitly enabled
- sampling windows < 5s and staggered so at most 1 worker per shard sampled
Maya: Ops playbook: if sampling triggers a perf regression alert, auto-disable sampling for 30m and create an incident ticket with traces.
Alex: Action items:
- Sam: add NVTX markers + feature flag (PR)
- Jorge: run cluster experiments with 0.5%, 1%, 2% budgets and collect overhead matrix
- Maya: draft guardrail doc and alert thresholds
- Devon: add KV miss annotations and ensure low-cost counters
Sam: Will do. I'll prototype NVTX wrapper in runtime today. :thumbsup:
Jorge: I'll take the 1%/2% experiments and share curves. :eyes:
Devon: I'll add the cache markers.
Maya: I'll draft the short ops doc and circulate.
Alex: Nice. If someone hits a surprising kernel selection in the traces ping me and include the perfetto link + nvtx timestamps.
infra-bot: [metric-bot] sampling-run metrics: cpu_overhead=1.4%, p95_delta=3ms, trace_size=12MB (2s window)
Sam: Great, that's within our target. We'll keep iterating.
